ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Irène Joliot-Curie

code.originalText: Count recovery and response assessment; cycle 2; transplant evaluation; occupational dose records

text.paragraph: Count recovery, response assessment, cycle 2, transplant planning, and her dose records. [S]

Mrs. Joliot-Curie returns on day 33, eleven days after venetoclax was stopped. She feels stronger, walks for half an hour, and has begun reading papers again. She has had no fever or bleeding. Her posaconazole trough level, drawn three days ago, was in the target range. The transplant center reports that the unrelated donor search has found two fully matched donors. Her employer's radiation safety office has acknowledged her request and is assembling her dose records, including the bioassay from the laboratory accident. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-30; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Fine crackles at the right apex, unchanged
Two months of tiredness, easy bruising and bleeding gums, with pancytopenia and 12 percent blasts on the blood smear; acute leukemia suspected and urgent hematology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the bone marrow diagnosis two days later; its timing echoes the documented decline in her health (D).

Acute myeloid leukemia diagnosed on bone marrow biopsy (34 percent myeloblasts), in a physicist with decades of occupational exposure to ionizing radiation; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to her documented leukemia
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and subtype; the type of her real leukemia is not documented.

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over about four decades: X-ray work early in her career, laboratory work with polonium and other radioactive sources, and a laboratory accident in which a sealed polonium source ruptured on her bench about ten years ago
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented occupational exposure.
Pulmonary tuberculosis in her forties, treated to completion; no symptoms of active disease
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented tuberculosis; the treatment details are synthetic.

Moderately reduced lung gas transfer (DLCO 58 percent of predicted, FEV1 76 percent) from old tuberculous scarring of the right upper lobe; with performance status 2, it makes her unfit for intensive induction
S — Synthetic finding on pre-treatment testing.
Nausea with vomiting and constipation on day 11 of cycle 1 of azacitidine with venetoclax, without fever, with mild low potassium; managed as an outpatient; resolved
S — Synthetic treatment side effect; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Acute myeloid leukemia after cycle 1 (C92.00). Neutrophils 0.9 and platelets 88 x10^3/uL with no circulating blasts, after a day-22 marrow with 3 percent blasts: complete remission with partial hematologic recovery (ELN 2022), with measurable residual disease still detectable. This is a good first response, but TP53-mutated leukemia often relapses, so the plan is to continue azacitidine with venetoclax and move to a reduced-intensity allogeneic transplant from a matched unrelated donor after two to three more cycles if remission holds. We discussed this plainly, with the numbers she asked for. [S]
Cycle 2 from today: azacitidine days 1 to 7 and venetoclax 70 mg on days 1 to 21.
Stop levofloxacin now that neutrophils are above 0.5; continue posaconazole and acyclovir.
Measurable residual disease marrow after cycle 2.
Transplant center visit to plan timing and conditioning.

Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation (Z57.1). Records requested and acknowledged; they will be reviewed with her and kept in the chart. [S]
Review the dose records when received.

list.item: Diagnosis, classification and a treatment decision within two weeks of the first visit. Outcome by 2026-09-28: Marrow two days after the first visit; genetics back and treatment started on day 14 [S]

Complete cycle 1 without tumor lysis, invasive fungal infection, or bleeding. Outcome by 2026-10-30: No tumor lysis; no fever or fungal infection; no bleeding beyond bruising; one outpatient visit for nausea [S]

Remission on the response assessment after cycle 1 (ELN 2022 complete remission, or complete remission with partial hematologic recovery). Outcome by 2026-10-30: Day-22 marrow blasts 3%; at day 33 neutrophils 0.9 and platelets 88: complete remission with partial hematologic recovery, measurable residual disease positive [S]

Her own goals and values recorded and her symptoms controlled with the palliative care team from the first cycle. Outcome by 2026-09-28: Seen by the palliative care team on day 1; goals recorded; symptoms reviewed at every visit [S]
Her occupational dose records obtained and the exposure history documented. Outcome by 2026-10-30: Records requested in writing from the employer's radiation safety office; history documented [S]
